{{Quote|Destiny has but one throne, and if the Jedi queen claims it, the Sith cannot.|Sarasu Taalon|<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>}}
The '''Throne of Balance''' was a site in the realm of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] known as [[beyond shadows]]. Viewable within the [[Pool of Knowledge]] on a [[Abeloth's planet|planet]] in [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]], it granted a vision of the future in the form of a being or beings on or around the Throne. Both [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] viewed the Throne of Balance. The first time Solo viewed it, he saw a [[Darth Krayt|dark, armored figure]] ruling [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and surrounded by [[One Sith|dark acolytes]], and became determined to prevent that future's fulfillment.<ref name="Abyss">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]''</ref> Shortly before he died, Solo saw the Throne of Balance again, except this time with his own daughter, [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana]], on the Throne, ruling justly in a time of peace.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

[[43 ABY|Two years later]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] had a similar vision of Allana Solo standing in front of a mix of [[Species/Legends|species]], looking to her for guidance and peace. In Organa Solo's vision, Allana was beside a large white throne, but no one was standing beside her to help her or comfort her, and none of the [[Skywalker family/Legends|Skywalkers]] or [[Solo family/Legends|Solos]] were there either.<ref name="Abyss" />

Luke Skywalker later looked upon the Throne of Balance while he was beyond shadows, and he too saw Allana ruling in a time of peace.<ref name="Abyss" /><ref name="Invincible" /> Later, [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[High Lord (Circle of Lords)|High Lord]] [[Sarasu Taalon]] saw a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Queen/Legends|queen]]&mdash;unbeknownst to him, Allana Solo&mdash;on the Throne, causing the [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Sith's]] alliance with the Jedi to [[Duel at the Pool of Knowledge|dissolve]]. He feared that she could prevent the Sith from retaking the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and thus desired to learn everything about her, so that he could ensure such circumstances did not come about.<ref name="Vortex" />

During the [[Duel at the Lake of Apparitions]], Luke finally met the Dark Man. After the two worked together to defeat [[Abeloth]], Jacen confided in Luke that the reason he turned to the dark side and became a Sith was in order to change the future because he had seen Allana next to the Dark Man on the Throne of Balance.<ref name="Apocalypse">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse]]''</ref> Krayt countered with his own correct speculation, that he would one day rule, and that Caedus's deeds only slowed him down.<ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The concept of the Throne of Balance was developed by [[Troy Denning]] in his ''[[Star Wars]]'' writing, from ''[[Star Wars: The Dark Nest Trilogy]]'' through to ''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]'' until it was first identified by name in ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]''. The author stated that it was not a physical throne, but a mythic symbol that readers should be careful of interpreting too literally.<ref name="Denning Facebook">{{Facebook|username=troy.denning|url=starwarsbooks/posts/10150727438248713|name=[[Troy Denning]]|date=2012-04-04|quote=Joseph, I think the question of whether Mortis is the homeworld of the Force really belongs to Dave Filoni to answer. In my view, it was a mythic interpretation of the Force functions -- but, as with all symbols, I think you have to be careful about reading it too literally.<br />[&hellip;]<br />Gregory -- exactly. The Throne of Balance is a symbol, not a physical throne. You have to think of it on several levels at once.<br />[&hellip;]<br />Candace -- I think the throne of balance was my idea. It kind of developed over time, from DN through Tempest.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/wip/detpL}}</ref>
